original_question: Which protein is encoded by the gene that is mutated in Norman-Roberts syndrome?

final_qi.question: Which protein is encoded by the gene that is mutated in Norman-Roberts syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Norman-Roberts syndrome (also called lissencephaly type 2) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the RELN gene located on chromosome 7q22. The RELN gene encodes reelin, a large secreted extracellular matrix glycoprotein that regulates neuronal migration and proper layering of the cerebral cortex and cerebellum. Thus, the mutated gene in Norman-Roberts syndrome produces the protein reelin.

final_answer.long_answer: Norman-Roberts syndrome (lissencephaly with cerebellar hypoplasia) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the RELN gene. RELN encodes reelin, a large secreted glycoprotein that guides neuronal migration and layering during brain development. Absence or reduction of reelin disrupts cortical and cerebellar architecture, producing the characteristic features of the syndrome.
